$comment: The Peninsula campaign's battles (Grognards Campaign Design doc, Peninsula battle sheets; maps in tools/maps/peninsula/maps.py). Built by tools/maps/peninsula/build.py.
name: The Peninsula
intro: 1808. Napoleon has put his brother on the throne of Spain, and Spain has risen. Britain sends an army to Portugal. Six years of war across the Peninsula follow, from Bailén to the walls of Toulouse.

battles.name: Bailén
battles.history: Dupont's corps, marching back north in the July heat, found Reding's Spaniards across its road at Bailén with Castaños closing behind. Four French attacks failed, the Swiss in French service went over to their countrymen, and Dupont surrendered nearly 18,000 men: the first defeat of a French army in the field.

objective.text: Hold Bailén, or a square of the ridge across the road, at the end of round 10.
Get a unit into Bailén, or break two Spanish Brigades, by the end of round 10.

battles.special: The Rumblar behind the French. Vedel arrives in round 8 behind the Spanish.

battles.name: Vimeiro
battles.history: Junot attacked Wellesley's army on the hills around Vimeiro in columns. British skirmishers and two-deep lines on the reverse slopes shot the columns to pieces, a flank attack on the eastern ridge was beaten back too, and Junot asked for terms.

objective.text: No French unit in Vimeiro village at the end of round 10.
Trant's Brigade unbroken at the end of round 10.
Get into Vimeiro village and remove three Allied units by the end of round 10.

battles.name: Somosierra
battles.history: San Juan's Spaniards held the Somosierra pass with four batteries stacked up the zigzag road in the fog. Napoleon sent the Polish Chevau-légers of the Guard straight up it; in minutes they rode over the batteries one after another, at terrible cost, and the road to Madrid lay open.

objective.text: Hold the summit, with both Brigades unbroken, at the end of round 10.
Get a unit onto the summit, or overrun two Spanish batteries, by the end of round 10.
Get a unit onto the summit, or overrun two Spanish batteries, by the end of round 10.

battles.name: The Death of General Colbert
battles.history: Covering Moore's winter retreat to Corunna, Paget's reserve held the bridge over the Cúa at Cacabelos. General Colbert led the French cavalry across and was shot dead by Rifleman Tom Plunket of the 95th at long range; the attack stalled and the rearguard got away.

objective.text: Have two units leave by the Villafranca road by the end of round 8.
Remove three British units by the end of round 8, with Colbert still in play.

needs: the marksman (the 95th's long shot at a commander)

battles.name: Corunna
battles.history: With the transports waiting in the harbour, Moore turned at Corunna to hold off Soult while the army embarked. Elviña was taken and retaken all afternoon; Moore was mortally wounded there, but the French were held and the army got away by sea that night.

objective.text: No French unit on the Monte Mero ridge, and none in Elviña, at the end of round 10.
Hold Elviña at the end of round 10, or break two British Brigades.

needs: the great battery fires over lower ground

battles.name: Talavera
battles.history: Wellesley and Cuesta stood side by side north of Talavera, the Spanish behind walls and olive groves, the British in the plain and on the Cerro de Medellín. Victor attacked the Medellín by night and again by day and failed; the Guards' counter-charge went too far and was nearly cut off, but the line held.

objective.text: No French unit on the Cerro de Medellín at the end of round 10.
Hold Talavera and its enclosures at the end of round 10.
Get a unit onto the Cerro de Medellín at any point, or have four units across the Portiña at the end of round 10.

battles.name: Ocaña
battles.history: Areizaga's large Spanish army, marching on Madrid, met Soult and King Joseph on the open plain at Ocaña. The Spanish infantry held the first attacks, but Sébastiani's cavalry swept round the Spanish right and the army broke: the worst Spanish defeat of the war.

objective.text: At least two Brigades unbroken at the end of round 10 (the army gets away).
Break one Spanish Brigade by the end of round 10.

battles.name: The Côa
battles.history: Craufurd kept the Light Division too long on the wrong bank of the Côa below Almeida, and Ney fell on it with his whole corps. The division fought its way back through the vineyards to the single bridge in the gorge and held it; three French attempts to storm the bridge were shot down.

objective.text: Three units across the Côa, and no French unit on the far end of the bridge, at the end of round 8.
A Caçador battalion across the Côa at the end of round 8.
Remove two Allied units, or get a unit over the bridge, by the end of round 8.

battles.name: Bussaco
battles.history: Masséna sent Reynier and Ney straight up the long, steep ridge of Bussaco in the morning mist. Reynier's columns reached the crest and were driven off; Ney's attack climbed into the Light Division, which rose from behind the crest and fired at a few paces. The Portuguese held as well as the British.

objective.text: No French unit on the crest of the ridge at the end of round 10.
Two Portuguese units still on the ridge at the end of round 10.
Get a unit onto the crest at any point, or remove four Allied units, by the end of round 10.

battles.name: Sabugal
battles.history: Wellington planned to trap Reynier at Sabugal, but fog and rain threw his columns out. Beckwith's brigade crossed alone and met Reynier's whole corps on a hill; it held off attack after attack, cavalry too, until the rest of the army came up out of the fog.

objective.text: Beckwith's Brigade on the hill (a unit on any square of it) at the end of round 8.
Their Brigadier still in play at the end of round 8.
Break two Allied Brigades, or clear the hill of Allied units, by the end of round 8.

battles.name: Albuera
battles.history: Soult swung round Beresford's right through the woods onto the hill held by Zayas's Spaniards, who stood. Colborne's brigade was caught in line in a hailstorm by the Vistula Lancers and destroyed; then the Fusilier Brigade went up the hill and fought it out with the French columns until they broke.

objective.text: No French unit on the southern hills at the end of round 10.
Zayas still in play, with his Brigade, at the end of round 10.
Hold Albuera village at the end of round 10.
Break one Allied Brigade, or have three units across the Albuera stream at the end of round 10.

battles.name: El Bodón
battles.history: Montbrun's cavalry caught Colville's brigade on the heights at El Bodón. The 5th Foot charged the cavalry and took back the guns; then the 5th and 77th, with the 21st Portuguese, formed squares and marched six miles back to Fuenteguinaldo with the French horse riding round them, and were never broken.

objective.text: Two units leave by the Fuenteguinaldo end by the end of round 10.
The 21st Line leaves by the Fuenteguinaldo end by the end of round 10.
Remove four Allied units by the end of round 10.

battles.name: Arroyo dos Molinos
battles.history: Hill marched through the night and rain and fell on Girard's division at dawn as it formed up to leave Arroyo dos Molinos. The 71st and 92nd came into the village with the pipes playing "Hey, Johnnie Cope"; Girard's men fled up the Sierra behind it, and most of the division was killed or taken.

objective.text: Two squares of the village held, and four French units removed, by the end of round 8.
Hold the Mérida road at the end of round 8.
Morillo still in play at the end of round 8.
Three units leave over the Sierra (the French edge) by the end of round 8.

battles.name: Salamanca
battles.history: Marmont, racing to cut Wellington off from Portugal, let his left wing stretch out along the heights south of Salamanca. Wellington struck: Pakenham hit the head of the column, Le Marchant's heavy dragoons rode down Maucune's infantry, and though Pack's Portuguese were thrown back from the Greater Arapile, they pinned its defenders. Forty thousand men were beaten in forty minutes.

objective.text: Break one French Brigade and remove four French units by the end of round 10.
A unit next to the Greater Arapile at the end of any round, and Pack in play at the end of round 10.
Two Brigades unbroken, and the Greater Arapile still French, at the end of round 10.

battles.name: García Hernández
battles.history: The day after Salamanca, Bock's heavy dragoons of the King's German Legion caught Foy's rearguard on a slope near García Hernández. A dying French horse fell into the front of a square, the dragoons rode through the gap and broke it, then broke a second: one of the few times cavalry broke formed infantry.

objective.text: Break two French infantry units by the end of round 8.
Three units leave by the French end by the end of round 8.

needs: the dead horse (one re-roll against a square)

battles.name: Vitoria
battles.history: King Joseph's army stood in the Zadorra valley west of Vitoria, with its baggage and the loot of five years jammed on the roads behind it. Wellington attacked from four directions over the Zadorra bridges and round the north; the French army broke and fled, leaving everything behind.

objective.text: Take the knoll of Arinez at any point, and break two French Brigades, by the end of round 12.
Hold a square of the Puebla heights at the end of round 12.
Two units across the Zadorra at the end of round 12.
Eight units leave by the road to France (the French edge) by the end of round 12.

needs: the baggage (stops Allied units for a round)

battles.name: Toulouse
battles.history: Soult held Toulouse behind the Garonne and the canal, with his strongest works on the Calvinet ridge. Freire's Spaniards attacked its northern end and were thrown back; Beresford marched along the marshy valley under fire and stormed the southern end. Napoleon had already abdicated: the news had not reached either army.

objective.text: Hold a southern redoubt at the end of round 12.
A unit next to the northern redoubts at the end of any round, and Freire still in play at the end of round 12.
Hold the northern redoubt, and have two Brigades unbroken, at the end of round 12.
